preamble: Velar fronting replaces velar stops with alveolars (/ɡ/ > [d], /k/ > [t]). It is one of the most frequent phonological processes in children acquiring English and is usually gone by about age 4. In positional velar fronting it applies only in prosodically strong positions, that is word-initial and stressed-syllable onsets, while codas and weak onsets keep the velar. Fronting is also more likely before front vowels. No regular diachronic sound change of plain [ɡ] to [d] is known. Historical velar-to-coronal shifts go through palatalization and end in affricates or sibilants (ɡ > dʒ, dz, z), and Greek δ from *gʷ involves a labiovelar.
